speeches.label: Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela
speeches.text: The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela has the honour to take the floor on behalf of the Group of Friends in Defense of the Charter of the United Nations. speeches.speaker: Mr. Hermida Castillo
speeches.label: Nicaragua
speeches.text: Nicaragua associates itself with the statement delivered just now by the brother Ambassador of Venezuela on behalf of the Group of Friends in Defense of the Charter of the United Nations. Today we gather to address a cause of freedom and divine justice that demands our most serious protection. For decades, we have denounced Israel’s illegal occupation, as well as its expansionist and militaristic policies, which undermine all efforts for dialogue to achieve peace. speeches.speaker: Mr. Alrowaiei
speeches.label: Bahrain
speeches.text: At the outset, we would like to express our gratitude to the President for convening this important discussion and to the secretariat of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development for its report (see A/79/343), transmitted by the Secretary -General, and the Chair of the Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People for its report (A/79/35), which are before us. speeches.label: Zimbabwe
speeches.text: We thank the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) for its report (see A/79/343), transmitted by the Secretary-General, and the Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People for its report (A/79/35) on the question of Palestine. speeches.speaker: Mr. Fogarty
speeches.label: United States of America
speeches.text: One-sided resolutions will not help advance a durable peace and bring us closer to a two-State solution. They only perpetuate long-standing divisions at a moment when we urgently need to work together. The United States will vote against the three draft resolutions before us today (A/79/L.19, A/79/L.23 and A/79/L.24), as they neither advance peace, nor create the conditions for direct negotiations between Israelis and Palestinians. The United States has continuously stressed our view that we need to end the conflict;

speeches.label: Plurinational State of Bolivia
speeches.text: We welcome the convening of this meeting. We align ourselves with the statement delivered on behalf of the Group of Friends in Defense of the Charter of the United Nations. We express our recognition to the Secretary-General for his ongoing efforts and the reports presented to the General Assembly, as well as to the President and the Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People, of which Bolivia is a member. speeches.label: Oman
speeches.text: The Palestinian question is an open wound for humanity, a matter of moral, political and legal significance that serves as a true test of the international community’s conscience and its ability to uphold justice. speeches.text: I would like to begin by expressing my sincere appreciation to the President of the General Assembly. Today, I am addressing the Assembly for the discussion of agenda item 34, entitled “The situation in the Middle East”, under which Egypt introduces a d raft resolution entitled “The Syrian Golan” every year. speeches.item_title: The situation in the Middle East

speeches.text: I thank the President for convening this crucial meeting on the situation in the Middle East. The Maldives welcomes draft resolution (A/79/L.19) and the Secretary-General’s report on this agenda (A/79/194). Both underscore the urgent need for justice, accountability and peace in a region entrenched in suffering and plagued by unresolved conflicts. speeches.item_title: The situation in the Middle East
speeches.text: Nicaragua expresses its profound concern regarding the situation in the Middle East, which has been ravaged by violence, interference in internal affairs, foreign aggression and protracted conflicts. The situation in Palestine is the hotbed of the conflict in that region. speeches.speaker: Mr. Alscher
speeches.label: Germany
speeches.text: Germany voted yes on the resolution entitled “Peaceful settlement of the question of Palestine” (resolution 79/81) as an expression of our long-standing position on the two-State solution. We firmly support a negotiated solution with two States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders. This framework is essential to achieve a just and lasting peace in the region. We support the call for international efforts to facilitate negotiations and encourage progress towards peace, but

speeches.speaker: Mr. Rae
speeches.label: Canada
speeches.text: Canada voted in favour of resolution 79/81 today in order to emphasize our significant concerns about the direction that the Israeli-Palestinian conflict has taken and to reaffirm our unwavering commitment to a solution based on the coexistence of two States, one in which the security interests of the Israelis and the Palestinians are recognized and respected. The heinous terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and the devastating humanitarian consequences of the conflict in Gaza are clearly a watershed moment for

speeches.speaker: Mr. Larsen
speeches.label: Australia
speeches.text: Australia’s vote today in favour of the resolution concerning the peaceful settlement of the question of Palestine (resolution 79/81) returns Australia to the position it took until 2001. The years leading up to that point was a time when the international community — and the parties themselves — came together to chart a path towards a two-State solution: a Palestinian State and the State of Israel, side by side, within safe, secure and internationally recognized borders. speeches.text: I have the honour to speak on behalf of the European Union and its member States.
